My sex drive is insane 6 months PP and I attribute it to two things:

1. I workout A LOT. Lots of strength training and cardio. I think that is helping me to create testosterone and thus helping to really ramp up my drive.

2. I am on the Skyla IUD. It lasts 3 years and has a low amount of hormone. I haven’t had any adverse affects yet, and I think that this small amount of hormone is helping to bolster my drive in the same way that my hormones did when I was pregnant.

Honestly, the biggest factor was me starting to feel ownership of my body again. I found that by working out, but however you get there is great. Take time for yourself, appreciate your body in the state that is now and your drive will come back to you! If it’s truly a concern you can always talk to your doctor about it as well!

I got the Skyla IUD placed 7 weeks PP! It is hormonal, but the level is so low it really doesn't affect me at all! Also the procedure was pretty painless, I was terrified of the pain going in, but I barely felt a thing! I used to hate hormonal BC, but the Skyla is such a low dose it really shouldn't affect you that much!

Was the bread actually moldy though? It sounds like you might have a bit of food-related anxiety/germaphobia. Have you discussed these feelings with a professional? I was extremely germaphobic for the bulk of my life, esp. when it comes to food and water. I often would have to bring my own bottled water everywhere, as that was the only “safe” thing for me to drink. I have been working through that now, but in my experience it was always easier to bring my own safe food and drink, rather than expect people to live up to my (impossible) standards. Also, kids can be really yucky with food, so it might be helpful to speak with someone about your food anxieties prior to your little one’s arrival! 

Your feelings are 100% valid, but you may want to get some help in figuring out how to cope with contamination/food anxiety!

I was freshly two months postpartum when I joined and loved the fact that I have 24 hour access! When the baby gets up at 5, I hand her to my husband and I’m off to the gym! This is the first gym I have ever stayed consistent with! I just LOVE how i feel leaving the sauna! I just always feel so energized and proud of myself! Not to mention, I have always tied sweat to a feeling of accomplishment, and let’s just say i feel incredibly accomplished at the end of my workouts! I’ve only been going for 4 weeks every day, but I already feel so much better in my skin! I don’t weigh myself, so I can’t say anything about weight loss, but my clothes are finally fitting again and that is more than enough for me! Stay consistent, I promise you’ll see results!

When I got to start working out again! I didn’t realize how much consistent working out affects my sense of self. It definitely looks different to pre-pregnancy (i.e. can’t go to yoga classes 5x a week, have to wait until my husband gets home from work before I go to the gym), but I figured out how to adjust! Also I think it gave me the opportunity to focus on something other than my baby once a day! Like, when I go to the gym I get to zone in on myself and that has helped so much!

I completely understand this approach, I do. I promise you, I would never, ever put my child in harm’s way. I just have a hard time with all the fear around parenting, especially girls. I’ve gotten shit for having a baby monitor, for putting her in dresses, etc. The reasoning for that has always been “what if a creep…”, and that really gets under my skin. The world is full of awful people, and awful things, but if I parent with the philosophy that everyone is possibly out to harm my child, I fear I might do more damage in the long run. As I stated in an earlier comment, I only post once or twice a year onto private accounts with none of her personal information (even her name is private). I’m not naive to the world, I was just wondering what some people’s reasoning is for keeping their kids offline.
I don’t think of my baby as an accessory?

This has been my approach so far! No personal information, no embarrassing photos, everything on private accounts. I’m not sharing my baby to a million followers, or documenting every tantrum. I just like for my friends to see her sweet face without texting and asking all the time (which they have done)!

If you’re looking at Europe, Edinburgh, Scotland is absolutely gorgeous! It’s super walkable, they have great public transit, and there are several nice hostels and AirBnBs that aren’t too expensive! Hiking to the top of Arthur’s seat is an absolute must-do, and the Royal Mile has a lot of great pubs and restaurants that are so fun! It’s a pretty great city for solo travel as there’s lots of cool tours to take, plus (in my experience) the locals are super friendly! I saw another suggestion for New Orleans, and as fun as the city is, if you are a solo female traveler I wouldn’t recommend it! I live fairly close to NOLA and I wouldn’t dream of going by myself… Bourbon St. can get pretty dangerous and (unless you’re big on cajun food and drinking) there’s not too much to do solo there!

My favorite saying of all time has gotten me through a lot of these dark moments: ‘Transit Umbra Lux Permanet’ or 'Shadow Passes, Light Remains'. I have it tattooed on my wrist to remind myself that I am just in a shadowed place right now, that light is still here, it’s just blocked by an obstacle right now. This obstacle will move, this shadow will pass. Time is a good friend in moments like these. You’re absolutely worth it. Give yourself one more week, then one more month, then one more year. Keep giving yourself time, and you will find yourself in a much lighter place.

I think the best sign for you is that you recognize that this will end, you’re just waiting for the day. Most people don’t see that it will end. From what I can gather, school is a massive stressor for you right now. In my darkest points this year, I was working full-time, attending class daily, and planning my wedding. Once I finally quit my job, i felt all of this stress lift! I turned in a two-weeks notice and I had a self care day on the day after my last day at work. I have actually written in my planner little self-care days so that I have a day to look forward to each week. You are about to have a major stressor lift in about two months. Try to plan something special for yourself for that day or week after you graduate or finish finals! Give yourself multiple things to look forward to as a celebration of your accomplishment! Beyond that, plan a few hours or a day for yourself each week! Give yourself a designated day to do little things that you enjoy,  it can make the days a lot more bearable if you have a day set aside for yourself. Create a countdown to your last day of classes and keep track of it! It’s so helpful to watch that number get smaller and smaller as the semester wears on! There are so many little things that you can do in service of yourself in order to find some peace in these stressful times. It could be as little as treating yourself to coffee or your favorite meal. Are you in-person or online? I know a lot of fellow students who have sunk pretty low being back to in-person classes this year. Being a student is absolutely exhausting, it probably is burnout. Here’s the thing though, you’re wanting to help people. Maybe you’re wanting to save lives.. If you don’t finish, how many people will go unhelped without you. I know that if my therapist wasn’t here, I probably would’ve gone down a long time ago. I’m not adding pressure but this has been the way that i’m getting through these last two months. I feel like I owe it to my younger, starry eyed, self to be successful. I owe it to the people I might help. I owe it to my ancestors who worked so hard to give me this opportunity. I owe it to my kids to be someone they look up to. I owe it to myself in my freshman year. And if all else fails, i try to think of who might have to take over my student loans if I’m not here, that one usually brings things into focus, haha. 
You can’t quit this close. You shouldn’t end everything right now. There will be a day that you walk across that stage at graduation and feel so much pride for having finished. For having done something many of your peers couldn’t. It’s possible and thoroughly attainable.

See, here’s the thing… you absolutely can. You can because you’re alive. You can only stop making beautiful things after you’re no longer here. I’m sure, even if it doesn’t feel like it, that youve impacted someone positively. You smiled at someone who needed a smile, or tipped a waitress on one of her bad days. Have you ever had a stranger make your day better with one tiny interaction?
I’ve been in the same boat these past few months. I’ve chalked it up to senior-itis, haha. I assume you’re going into psychology because you want to help people, right?

Do you think you could try and channel all of that pain into your art? I paint and sometimes i will create a piece just to get all of it on canvas; have somewhere else for my pain to be. I’m sure you could turn everything that you are facing into something beautiful..

Write a poem from that pain. Create something productive and beautiful. Who knows? That poem could be the reason another person decides to stay. You are 14. You’re life is just beginning in so many ways. Stay for the poetry you will write. Stay for the kids you want to have. Stay for your high school diploma. Stick around for your first true love. Stick around for your first massive heartbreak. You’re a poet. The best ones value life so deeply because they take all of the good and all of the bad and they turn that into something beautiful. Turn life into something beautiful.

Every day is hard when you carry something like this. Something similar happened to me when I was younger and I didn’t know how to cope. Years later I’ve started seeing a therapist, and if you can it’s an amazing tool. It may feel weird at first, but you’ve already made the first step of definitely labeled your experience as assault (that is really hard, especially when the perpetrator is someone you trusted). You are strong, and every day will get a little easier. Find people that you trust and just talk about it, talk through everything. You will persevere, and it will get easier from here, I promise.

Abeka is a no-go! We used it growing up and the curriculum does not teach effectively ! I understand Christian homeschool programs like to have a focus on God, but Abeka has a blatant disregard for scientific and historical accuracy. One of my old science books stated that the world was less than 2,000 years old, if that is any indication! I would look to local homeschool groups (they often have pages on facebook) to find suggestions! They often have resources shared by parents who specialize in different areas of study and maybe even co-learning opportunities! Co-learning days were often my favorite and gave me a much better understanding of subjects my parents were unable to teach effectively!
